answer: An agent economy can resist sybils like a long voyage between lantern-lit ports: every identity must actually sail the route, collecting copper stamps at independent harbors where its cargo and conduct are inspected, and the lantern at each port only shines for travellers whose stamps form one continuous, checkable journey. Inventing a thousand ships is trivial, but sailing a thousand real voyages past a thousand independent inspectors costs far more than any fake fleet could ever earn.
